risks.note: MD&A: radio industry revenues fell 7% in 2025 to approximately ₹2,300 crore; ad volumes grew only 2% while ad yields fell 9% and inventory transitioned from high-yield metro markets to smaller towns. The Outlook says revenues are expected to remain largely flat near term and could decline to ₹2,200 crore by 2028 if structural challenges persist. The industry 'remains under pressure and continues to operate below its long-term potential'.
risks.risk: Structural contraction of the radio advertising market

risks.note: MD&A: radio's effectiveness as an advertising medium 'is being challenged by the rapid growth of digital audio platforms and streaming services, alongside the absence of FM receivers in many smartphones and newer car models' - a distribution risk the broadcaster cannot control.
risks.risk: Substitution by digital audio platforms, plus loss of the physical receiver base

risks.note: Revenue from operations is described as Advertisement Revenue from FM broadcasting, so the P&L is levered to one ad medium in one country. PROVENANCE: the Directors' Report (governance bundle) confirms the Company has no Subsidiary, Joint Venture or Associate Company, so there is no diversified entity structure to absorb the cycle. No Risks & Concerns section was routed into this bundle.

MD&A: national advertisers, especially FMCG, reduced spends while retail advertisers became key contributors (in some cases up to 75% of ad volumes); over 12,700 brands advertised in 2025 but the number of advertisers declined for the second consecutive year, reflecting fragmentation of media budgets. Services, auto and BFSI account for over half of ad volumes - a further concentration point.
risks.risk: Advertiser-base erosion and mix shift away from national/FMCG spends

risks.note: MD&A: non-FCT revenue is the designated growth driver (around 25% of industry revenue, projected up to 39% by 2028), but 'while event-led revenues have grown, margins remain relatively modest (10-15%), necessitating further innovation in monetisation models'. Growth in the pivot does not restore the economics of the legacy business.
risks.risk: The diversification path itself is margin-dilutive

risks.note: MD&A: 'the sector saw shutdown of a few private stations due to financial unviability, underscoring the economic stress within the industry', and FM auctions drew a muted response with only 62 licences sold across 43 cities. Licence fees are a standing cost of operating stations regardless of yield.

The Chairman explicitly flags that 'the challenging revenue environment, coupled with an impairment charge of ₹49 crores, led to a net loss of ₹53.3 crores during the year compared to a net loss of ₹33.8 crores in FY25'. PROVENANCE: Chairman's Insight, routed to the profile/strategy_outlook bundles, not to this one. A second consecutive year of impairment is a structural signal on the recoverable value of the station/intangible base.

Operating performance for the year: digital revenue declined 53% after 36% growth in the previous year, and digital channels contributed 7% of revenue against 11% in FY25 - the diversification engine is not yet a stable base. PROVENANCE: Key Performance Indicators page, routed to the profile/strategy_outlook bundles.
risks.risk: Volatility of the digital revenue stream the strategy depends on
